requirements.title: The application shall display a current-streak badge on every habit row

vision.paraphrase: The streak number is the visual hero of every row — always present.

conops.paraphrase: A brand-new habit renders with streak 0, so the badge exists from the first row.

requirements.title: The application shall compute the current streak as the count of consecutive completed local calendar days ending today, when today is completed

vision.paraphrase: The normative streak rule: consecutive days ending today when today is completed.

conops.paraphrase: Checking today off extends the visible run to include today.

requirements.title: The application shall keep the streak visible without reset when today is not yet completed but yesterday is

vision.paraphrase: The yesterday-grace clause: an unchecked day still shows the streak until the day truly ends.

conops.paraphrase: Opening the app the next morning still shows yesterday's streak before the check-in.

requirements.title: The application shall display a streak of 0 when neither today nor yesterday is completed

vision.paraphrase: The zero clause of the streak rule: a missed day honestly resets the count.

conops.paraphrase: The user who skipped days sees 0 — the number tells the truth, no guilt mechanics.

requirements.title: The application shall update the streak badge immediately when "Done today" is toggled, without a page reload

vision.paraphrase: Serves goal G3 — the streak a row displays answers to today's check-in in the same instant it happens, never a step behind.

conops.paraphrase: The count climbs 0 → 1 on the already-drawn page the moment the user clicks "Done today" — feedback arrives without any reload.

requirements.title: The application shall recompute a restored habit's streak from its preserved completion history

vision.paraphrase: Archive/restore preserves completions, so streak logic applies unchanged after restore.

conops.paraphrase: A restored habit shows its history-derived streak — alive if yesterday or today counts, else 0.

requirements.title: The application shall display a "DAY STREAK" caption beneath the streak number in every habit row's streak badge

vision.paraphrase: The MVP defines the row's streak badge as a labeled count rather than a bare number, so the motivating figure reads with its meaning at a glance.

The design direction pairs the hero number with a caption set directly under it, making every row's streak self-describing instead of relying on the user to guess what the figure counts; it further specifies the caption is set in the design system's mono caption style, which this TOR pins alongside the caption's presence and placement.

conops.paraphrase: The to-be row anatomy is fixed as name, streak badge with its "DAY STREAK" caption beneath the number, Done toggle, and Archive/Restore action — the caption is part of every row's structure, not an optional flourish.
Even a brand-new habit's very first row shows the caption under its zero streak, so the badge format is established from the user's first encounter with the list.

requirements.title: The application shall display a help hint above the habit list on the Active view explaining streak continuation and the honest reset, and shall not display it on the Archived view

vision.paraphrase: The MVP's list specification reserves a single-line hint above the Active list that teaches how streaks continue and what a missed day costs.
The design direction positions the streak-rule hint where it is read before the first check-in, teaching the honest-reset rule up front rather than letting the user discover it through a lost streak.

conops.paraphrase: The hint is on screen from the very first boot of the app, so a first-time visitor meets the streak rule before any habit — or any streak — exists.

The functional summary lists the one-line Active-view hint as its own capability whose job is teaching the honest-reset rule; this TOR makes that observable, including its absence once the user switches to Archived.
